calibration_notice: This profile contains helper-level body plans and remains available only for historical calibration. Do not use it for formal blind-first runs.

kbuild.rust_config_prompt: Rust reference driver for Asix PHYs
rust_help: Uses the Rust reference driver for the Asix PHY family (ax88796b_rust.ko).
The intent is to stay within the current safe PHY abstraction subset.

translation.goal: Constrain a strict blind-first `drivers/net/phy/ax88796b_rust.rs` candidate to a minimal, artifact-driven Rust PHY driver covering registration, `read_status`, `suspend`, `resume`, `soft_reset`, and `link_change_notify` for the Asix family.
translation.abstraction_goal: Keep the driver inside the existing safe PHY abstraction while covering the three Asix variants without driver-side `unsafe`, direct `bindings::*`, or reference-driver leakage.

mvp_scope.note: The strict blind-first acceptance target is build plus lifecycle validation through the fallback oracle until a trusted PHY KUnit runner lands.

body_plan: Call `dev.genphy_update_link()?` and bail out early if the link is down.
Read `C22::BMCR` through the safe PHY register API and update speed/duplex on the Rust device.
Use `dev.genphy_read_lpa()?` and resolve autonegotiation through the safe abstraction only.

phy_driver.soft_reset.rust_surface: impl Driver for PhyAX88772A::soft_reset / PhyAX88772C::soft_reset / PhyAX88796B::soft_reset
body_plan: Keep the Asix-specific reset sequence in a local helper that writes `C22::BMCR` and then calls `dev.genphy_soft_reset()`.
Check `dev.state()` and only trigger `dev.init_hw()` plus `dev.start_aneg()` when the PHY is in `DeviceState::NoLink`.

driver_generation_rules: Read only the current experiment artifacts plus the allowlisted generic PHY abstraction files before writing driver code.
Do not read, diff, or quote the upstream Rust reference driver or any archived blind benchmark report before the experiment is frozen.
Use `rust/kernel/net/phy.rs` and `rust/kernel/net/phy/reg.rs` only as the generic safe abstraction surface; keep all module-specific logic constrained by the generated artifact set.
If the artifact and safe PHY abstraction are insufficient, stop and record a planner/profile or abstraction gap instead of filling it with driver-side `unsafe`.

private_state.note: The strict blind-first Asix Rust PHY driver should not introduce per-device Rust private state.
